title.narrative: Community-based outbreak control measures to limit transmission of ebola outbreak in Sierra Leone.

description.narrative:
The first case of Ebola in Sierra Leone was reported on 25th May 2014. To date (27th July 2014), the Ebola outbreak has been reported in every district with 305 confirmed positive cases and 182 deaths. This is the most severe outbreak of Ebola every recorded and continues to spread.
Denial and resistance from the communities, as well as myths and false information are some of the major challenges in stemming the spread of the virus. This project represents CAFOD's contribution to Caritas Sierra Leone's CI appeal (EA 21/2014) and is in addition to the £6,000 already committed (Project ref: SLN160).
-Improve knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) on Ebola transmission prevention through training and public sensitization. -Improve hygiene/sanitation practices through the provision of hygiene kits. -Engage traditional leaders and promote dialogue amongst local communities to dispel some of the myths of Ebola.
The project aims to reach a total of 61,965 direct beneficiaries and 180,000 indirect beneficiaries. This project will contribute towards this total beneficiary number.
This project funding represents approximate 7% of the total EA budget and is unearmarked.
